name: Pre-computed Color/Opacity Volume Rendering
aliases: Pre-computed Color/Opacity Volume Rendering — Levoy's method
definition: A modification of image order algorithms where a color and opacity volume are pre-computed from the original dataset to avoid per-ray shading/classification, at the cost of requiring recomputation when parameters change.
summary: Pre-computed Color/Opacity Volume Rendering precomputes opacity and shaded color fields to enable fast, view-independent rendering by moving expensive classification and shading calculations into a one-time preprocessing step.
